title: Parse Watch Session Timestamps
prompt: You are working with a streaming video service modeled on public media consumption datasets (Nielsen, FCC). The sessions table tracks raw watch events with messy timestamp strings and contains columns for user_id, session_start_raw (a text timestamp that may have leading/trailing spaces), video_id, and minutes_watched. The session_start_raw column stores timestamps as VARCHAR in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS' but often includes extra whitespace. Write a query that cleans each session_start_raw value, extracts the watch month name, calculates how many whole days have passed between session_start and a reference cutoff date of '2024-12-01', and truncates the cleaned timestamp to the start of its day. Return one row per session with columns: session_id, clean_start (the trimmed timestamp cast to TIMESTAMP), month_name (the full month name from clean_start), days_ago (whole days from clean_start to '2024-12-01'), and day_start (clean_start truncated to midnight). Order the results by session_id.

display.context: You are working with a streaming video service modeled on public media consumption datasets.
display.task: Write a query that cleans each session_start_raw value, extracts the watch month name, calculates how many whole days have passed between session_start and a reference cutoff date, and truncates the cleaned timestamp to the start of its day.

table_notes.sessions: Tracks raw watch events with messy timestamp strings, user identifiers, video identifiers, and watch duration in minutes

output_field_notes.session_id: The unique identifier for each watch session
output_field_notes.clean_start: The session start timestamp after removing extra whitespace and converting to TIMESTAMP type
output_field_notes.month_name: The full name of the month when the session started
output_field_notes.days_ago: The number of whole days from the session start to the cutoff date of December 1, 2024
output_field_notes.day_start: The session start timestamp truncated to midnight of that day

field_logic: clean_start: remove leading and trailing whitespace from session_start_raw and convert the result to a TIMESTAMP
month_name: extract the full month name from the cleaned timestamp
days_ago: compute the whole-day difference between the cutoff date and the cleaned session start
day_start: truncate the cleaned timestamp to the beginning of its day
edge_cases: If session_start_raw has leading or trailing spaces, they must be removed before conversion.
If session_start_raw is NULL, the cleaned timestamp and derived fields will be NULL.
display.filter_note: All rows from the sessions table are included in the output.
display.order_by_note: Results are ordered by session_id in ascending order.

schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE sessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT, session_start_raw VARCHAR(50), video_id INT, minutes_watched INT);

composite_moves: row-transform: TRIM whitespace from VARCHAR timestamp
row-transform: cast cleaned string to TIMESTAMP
row-transform: TO_CHAR to extract month name
row-transform: date subtraction for whole days

hints: Start by removing any leading or trailing whitespace from the raw timestamp column.
Use TRIM to clean the string, then cast it to a TIMESTAMP type. Extract the month name using TO_CHAR with the 'FMMonth' format.
Calculate the whole-day difference by subtracting the cleaned timestamp (cast to DATE) from DATE '2024-12-01'. Truncate the cleaned timestamp to the day level using DATE_TRUNC('day', ...).
answer_key: SELECT session_id, TRIM(session_start_raw)::TIMESTAMP AS clean_start, TO_CHAR(TRIM(session_start_raw)::TIMESTAMP, 'FMMonth') AS month_name, DATE '2024-12-01' - TRIM(session_start_raw)::TIMESTAMP::DATE AS days_ago, DATE_TRUNC('day', TRIM(session_start_raw)::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start FROM sessions ORDER BY session_id;

_meta.scenario: a streaming video service tracking watch time and binge depth
